issues.legal_issue: Extraordinary writ jurisdiction is not an appropriate means to resolve a material dispute about the factual basis for a statutory royalty demand.
material_facts: The claimant sought constitutional writ relief against a demand for royalty on mined gypsum.
The applicable royalty rate depended on whether the gypsum met a specified purity threshold.
The claimant asserted that the gypsum was below the threshold, while the respondents disputed that claim and said adequate laboratory analysis had not been furnished.
A revision challenging the higher royalty rate had been dismissed by the central government.
issues.conclusion: The court upheld the refusal of writ relief because the gypsum’s purity was a question of fact and found no cogent ground to take a different view from the High Court.
issues.legal_principle: The royalty rate under Section 9(2) of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957, read with the relevant entry in the Second Schedule, depended on the gypsum’s purity. Determining that purity was a question of fact, and the court upheld the High Court’s refusal to resolve that disputed factual matter in extraordinary jurisdiction under Articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.constitutional_writ_proceeding: A claimant sought extraordinary constitutional review of an administrative demand.
predicates.disputed_material_fact: The claimant and the government disputed a factual characteristic that determined the amount of the demand.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks extraordinary constitutional review and the demand turns on a disputed material fact, the rule means that writ relief is refused.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant may not pursue parallel remedies concerning the same matter at the same time.
material_facts: After the High Court dismissed the writ petition, the claimant filed a suit raising the same question that had been the subject of the writ petition.
The suit had been dismissed in default, and an application to restore it was pending; the respondents stated that they would not oppose restoration.
issues.conclusion: The court held that the claimant could not pursue two parallel remedies concerning the same matter at the same time and dismissed the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: A party cannot pursue two parallel remedies in respect of the same matter at the same time. The court relied on no statutory provision or earlier case for this proposition.

predicates.appeal_from_writ_dismissal: A claimant appealed after a court dismissed the claimant’s writ petition.
predicates.same_issue_suit_pending: The claimant had filed a suit raising the same issue, and that suit or an application to restore it remained before the trial court.

issues.definition: When a claimant appeals the dismissal of a writ petition while a suit concerning the same issue remains before the trial court, the rule means that the remedies cannot be pursued simultaneously.
